The proposed solution's work gives $L = 4\pi$, but it then states "Final answer: 3," which does not follow from its own computation.

The derivation is correct up to that point. $f'(\theta) = i e^{i\theta}(1+e^{i\theta})^2$, so $|f'(\theta)| = 2(1+\cos\theta)$, and $\int_0^{2\pi} 2(1+\cos\theta)\,d\theta = 4\pi$. The total arc length of the curve is $4\pi$.

The curve is not simple, so $4\pi$ is not the perimeter of the enclosed region either. It crosses itself at $f(2\pi/3) = f(4\pi/3) = -2/3$, and it has a cusp at $\theta = \pi$ where $f'(\pi) = 0$. The small inner loop, for $\theta \in [2\pi/3, 4\pi/3]$, has length $4\pi/3 - 2\sqrt{3}$. Removing it leaves the outer boundary of length $8\pi/3 + 2\sqrt{3} \approx 11.84$, which is the boundary of the region in the sense of the problem.

Under either reading (total arc length $4\pi$ or outer boundary $8\pi/3 + 2\sqrt{3}$), the answer is not 3.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
